findings.status: suggested assumption clarification; examples and exercise are already finite with positive costs
findings.finding: The asymmetric-cost quantile passage differentiates expected loss and divides by c_u+c_o without explicitly stating the cost and integrability assumptions. The intended positive finite shortage/excess costs and finite conditional first moment are clear in the numerical exercise but should be stated for the general derivative claim.
findings.recommended_change: Precede the derivation with 'For positive finite c_u and c_o and E[|Y| | X=x] < infinity...' (or an appropriately qualified nonnegative-cost version). This avoids an undefined zero-total-cost ratio or differentiation of an infinite expectation.

formula_and_concept_review.risk_identity: Conditional test-average expectation follows from fixed-rule conditioning and matching test marginals; the manuscript correctly separates independence needed for ordinary variance calculations from the expectation identity. Independent new-outcome assumptions and finite second moments are explicit for the bias/noise/training-variance expansion. Cross-validation training-size and chronological-regime limitations are correctly distinguished.
formula_and_concept_review.loss_and_selection: MAE/MSE/RMSE dimensions and ranking claims are correct. Brier scores are0.25 and0.41. The finite two-candidate selection construction has expected minimum9 versus fixed candidate risk10. The pointwise minimum inequality and its comparison with the selected true risk are valid for the stated fixed candidate risks and finite expectations without candidate-score independence. The manuscript does not incorrectly generalize this to arbitrary random risk definitions.
formula_and_concept_review.split_roles: Training, validation and final test information roles are consistently separated. Feature selection, imputation and tuning are required to occur inside permitted splits; nested evaluation and group-versus-time targets are explained appropriately. The text correctly distinguishes a whole predeclared updating procedure from a fixed fitted vector and does not treat later test outcomes as forbidden forever when they become valid past inputs.
formula_and_concept_review.uncertainty: Paired loss differences retain covariance from common cases. The iid SE premise is explicit and not applied automatically to four chronological losses, overlapping horizons or folds with shared training histories. Limited test cases and possible distribution changes are acknowledged; no causal or trading-profit guarantee is asserted.

temporal_and_code_checks.reference_vs_release: history_as_of requires both period<=origin and released<=origin, sorted by reference period. forecast receives only eligible history and target, and drift uses elapsed target-minus-latest-reference distance. No target actual is passed into forecast. evaluate adds actual outcomes only for retrospective scoring and rejects labels not released by scored_as_of.
temporal_and_code_checks.selection_vs_test: Validation is scored at the recorded boundary and candidate selection with deterministic naive/mean/drift tie order precedes final-loss construction. Updating and fixed-origin final experiments use separately appropriate history. The same final comparison candidates are reported without changing selected_method. Final scoring may wait until all labels mature; this is separated from the earlier prediction origins.

temporal_and_code_checks.contracts: Exact unit/MSE/candidate-order validation matches report labels. Unique complete period keys, integer nonnegative demand and valid delayed release indices are checked. Fewer than two eligible records refuses the complete comparison even though a standalone naive rule could need fewer; this stricter common-comparison contract is documented. Internal helpers assume validated inputs, as the README states. Original files are read-only and default lookup is relative to the script.
